ui.aboutCredits: Built with FastAPI, docker-py, ruamel.yaml, APScheduler, Alpine.js, Tailwind CSS, marked, DOMPurify, Plus Jakarta Sans and JetBrains Mono — see the third-party licenses. App icon by boystyle2010.
ui.aboutIssues: Report a bug / request a feature
ui.aboutLicenseText: Free to use, copy, modify and distribute, provided the copyright notice and license are kept. Provided "as is", without warranty of any kind.
ui.aboutTagline: Fast, safe Docker & CasaOS app manager: real digest update checks, changelogs, release channels, compose editing and automatic rollback.
ui.allUpToDateToast: All apps are up to date ✓
ui.apSafe: Only images and build cache. Containers and volumes are never cleaned automatically.
ui.apiCounts: Last hour: {r} request(s) • {c} answered from cache
ui.apiPausedHelp: Checks for this source wait until then; the last known status is kept.
ui.apiSourcesDesc: Docker Hub and GitHub limit how many requests one IP can make. AppManager caches answers and pauses a source when it is limited, keeping the last known update status.
ui.autoPruneDesc: Automatically clean unused Docker data on a schedule
ui.autoRollbackDesc: If the new version crashes, restore the previous one automatically
ui.autoUpdateAppDesc: Update automatically on your daily schedule
ui.bkDesc: Archives the app's config files (.tar.gz) before each update
ui.bkNote: Scope: config files only (json, yaml, conf, env, small DBs, certificates…) in volumes mounted from /DATA/AppData. Data folders, media, logs and caches are skipped; files above the per-file limit are skipped. On a failed update, the previous image and docker-compose.yml are restored first; this backup is applied only if the previous version still fails to start.
ui.bkTitle: Back up app data before updates
ui.ccConfirm_http: The next check asks Docker Hub / GitHub again for every app. Nothing else changes.
ui.ccConfirm_resources: The CPU / RAM charts start empty again. Apps are not affected.
ui.ccConfirm_sso: AppManager downloads the provider settings and signing keys again at the next sign-in.
ui.ccConfirm_ui: Only this device: theme color, text size, corners, icons, app icon and the sign-in page light go back to the defaults.
ui.ccConfirm_updates: Saved changelogs and errors are removed, then all apps are checked again. Versions, update rules and history are kept.
ui.ccIntro: Copies AppManager keeps so pages open fast and Docker Hub / GitHub are not asked again and again. Clearing a cache never touches your apps, their data or your settings — the copies are simply fetched again. You rarely need it: use the tips below.
ui.ccUiDesc: Reload the newest interface — use it when the Home Screen app still shows an old look after an update. Keeps sign-in, settings and Web Push.
ui.ccUiResetDesc: Theme color, text size, corners, icons, app icon and the sign-in page light go back to the defaults on this device.
ui.ccWhen_docker: the SSD is getting full — old image versions and build leftovers are often the biggest items.
ui.ccWhen_http: a new version was just published but AppManager does not see it yet, or after adding / changing a registry account.
ui.ccWhen_resources: the CPU / RAM charts show odd spikes (for example after moving to new hardware) and you want them to start fresh.
ui.ccWhen_sso: single sign-on fails right after you changed the client, redirect address or signing keys on the provider.
ui.ccWhen_ui: the app on the Home Screen or the browser still shows an old design after AppManager was updated, or a button / page looks broken.
ui.ccWhen_uireset: you experimented with colors, text size or corners and want the original look back quickly.
ui.ccWhen_updates: a changelog looks wrong, empty or belongs to another version, or an old error message keeps showing.
ui.cc_docker_desc: Free SSD space in Storage & SSD (shows what will be removed first).
ui.cc_http_desc: Saved registry / GitHub answers ({n} · {s}). Clear to fetch fresh data right away (uses more API quota).
ui.cc_resources_desc: {n} measurements (last 7 days) used by the Task Manager charts.
ui.cc_sso_desc: Saved provider settings and signing keys ({n}). Clear after changing something on the provider side.
ui.cc_updates_desc: Saved release notes of {n} apps. Cleared and checked again; versions and update rules (wait N days) are kept.
ui.cfgFileFrom: Made by AppManager {v} on {d} ({h}). Choose what to restore:
ui.cfgNotIncluded: Not included: app data and app configuration backups (Settings → Storage & SSD), update history, activity log, caches.
ui.cfgPwShort: The backup password must be at least 8 characters
ui.cfgPwWarn: Keep this password safe: without it the file cannot be opened, and nobody can recover it.
ui.cfgRestoreLoseMe: Your account is not in this file: you will be signed out and must sign in with an account from the file.
ui.cfgRestoreMsg: Replace: {s}. The current configuration is saved first.
ui.cfgSafetyDesc: Automatic copies made before each restore (last 5), encrypted with the password used for that restore.
ui.cfgSignedOut: Your sign-in changed with the restored accounts — going to the login page…
ui.cfgTooBig: The file is larger than 20 MB
ui.cfgWhat: One file with accounts and roles (passwords stay hashed), SSO, API Tokens, notification channels, other servers, registry accounts, per-app update rules and general settings — to move to a new machine, reinstall or go back to an earlier setup. The file is encrypted with your password (scrypt + AES-256-GCM).
ui.cfgWill: The current configuration is saved automatically first (you can download it below to undo). The chosen parts are replaced by the file; other parts and app data stay as they are. Restoring accounts may sign you out.
ui.channelPreviewNote: {ch} channel selected (:{tag}). The changelog below is for the {ch} channel, version {ver}. Nothing is changed until you tap the update button.
ui.checkAlreadyRunning: An update check is already running…
ui.checksumOnlyNotes: This release only lists checksums and has no release notes. See GitHub ↗
ui.chooseVersionDesc: Switch to another recent version (newer or older)
ui.clearCacheDesc: Reload the newest interface (keeps sign-in, settings and Web Push)
ui.composeDuplicateMsg: The container runs from the file above and changes are saved there. The file(s) below differ; if CasaOS or the Terminal starts the app from them, these changes are lost and the app may break. Keep only one copy.
ui.composeDuplicateTitle: This app has another, different compose file
ui.confirmBatchMsg: apps will be updated sequentially and restarted briefly. Continue?
ui.confirmKillMsg: will be killed immediately (SIGKILL) without graceful shutdown. Unsaved data may be lost.
ui.confirmPruneMsg: Selected unused Docker resources will be permanently removed to free SSD space.
ui.confirmRestartMsg: will restart briefly and active connections may be interrupted.
ui.confirmRollbackMsg: Restore backup file and recreate container immediately?
ui.confirmStopMsg: will be stopped and become unreachable until started again.
ui.confirmUpdateMsg: Pull the latest image and recreate
ui.convertConfirmMsg: The old container is stopped and renamed, the app is started from the new docker-compose.yml and checked. On success the old container is removed (volumes and data kept); on failure the old container is restored.
ui.convertNote: Named volumes are kept as external, so the data stays the same. The old container is stopped and kept until the new one runs correctly; if the new one fails, the old one is started again.
ui.convertOptional: Optional: manage it with a docker-compose.yml
ui.convertOptionalMsg: AppManager already updates this docker run container directly. Converting is optional: it generates a docker-compose.yml from the container's current settings so you can manage it as a compose app. Review it below; nothing changes until you convert.
ui.copyManual: Cannot copy automatically: select the text and copy it
ui.customizeUpdateAllDesc: Choose which apps "Update All" updates. Unchecked apps are skipped (they can still be updated one by one). The choice is remembered; by default all apps are updated.
ui.dataApplyMsg: These folders are added as volumes to AppManager's docker-compose.yml, then AppManager restarts (a few seconds). If the new configuration does not start, the previous docker-compose.yml is restored automatically.
ui.dataFoldersIntro: Folders on the server that AppManager can read (mounted with the same path). Apps whose docker-compose.yml is inside them can be updated and edited.
ui.dataManualDesc: Type the folder path on the host
ui.dataManualHelp: Host folder that contains your apps' folders (each with its docker-compose.yml), e.g. /DATA/AppData or /opt/stacks.
ui.dataMissingCount: AppManager cannot read the compose file of {n}/{total} apps
ui.dataNoCompose: AppManager was not started with Docker Compose, so it cannot edit its own configuration. Add these lines under volumes: of AppManager and recreate it:
ui.dataNoResults: No folder with docker-compose files was found. Try Manual.
ui.dataResultsMsg: Folders found. Select the ones to add to AppManager:
ui.dataScanWarning: Auto Scan reads the whole server disk (read-only) and can take a long time if your server holds a lot of data.
ui.dataScanning: Scanning the server for docker-compose files…
ui.dataSetupMsg: AppManager reads each app's docker-compose.yml and settings at the same path as on the host, so the folder that holds your apps (e.g. /DATA/AppData) must be mounted into AppManager. Add it manually or let AppManager find it.
ui.deployAppIdOptional: App ID / Folder Name (optional if YAML has name:)
ui.deployCasaosHint: Saves directly to CasaOS apps folder for seamless Dashboard sync
ui.dfAddIntro: Enter the folder on the server that holds your apps (their docker-compose.yml). AppManager mounts it with the same path, so their compose files can be read.
ui.dfAlreadyAdded: This folder is already added (or inside an added folder)
ui.dfFound: Found {n} docker-compose file(s) in this folder
ui.dfNoCompose: AppManager was not started with Docker Compose, so folders cannot be changed here. Change the -v options in its docker run command.
ui.dfPlanAdd: Add {p} to AppManager (same path inside the container)
ui.dfPlanBackup: App backups use this folder; AppManager will use the new folder for app backups
ui.dfPlanFound: {n} docker-compose file(s) found in the new folder
ui.dfPlanLost: {n} app(s) will no longer be updatable or editable until their folder is added again: {apps}
ui.dfPlanNoDelete: Nothing is deleted or moved on the disk — only what AppManager can read changes
ui.dfPlanRestart: AppManager restarts (about 30 seconds); if it fails to start, the previous docker-compose.yml is put back automatically
ui.dfSelfNote: This folder holds AppManager's own docker-compose.yml, so it cannot be removed; a new path must still contain it.
ui.downgradeWarning: This is an older version than the one running. Some apps cannot read data written by a newer version; if it fails to start, the current version is restored automatically.
ui.dupComposeBadge: This app has more than one docker-compose file — tap to review
ui.dupComposeSkippedBadge: This app still has more than one docker-compose file (warning skipped; it reappears if a file changes). Merge to keep a single configuration.
ui.dupMergeMsg: The running (working) file is kept as the base; only extension blocks it lacks (x-casaos: title, icon, port) are taken from the other file. Both files are then identical; previous versions are saved as .bak. Allowed only while the container runs correctly; no container is recreated.
ui.enableAutoUpdateDesc: Only updates apps with Auto-Update toggled ON
ui.encDesc_bark: AES — only the Bark app on your iPhone can read the messages (not api.day.app or any Bark server).
ui.encDesc_webhook: AES-256-GCM — only your server with the key can read the messages.
ui.encHow_bark: In the Bark app: Settings → Push Encryption → Algorithm AES256 (32-character key; AES128 = 16, AES192 = 24), Mode CBC, Padding PKCS7, then enter the same Key and IV and save. Without it the iPhone cannot show the messages.
ui.encHow_webhook: The body becomes {"encrypted": base64(nonce 12 bytes + ciphertext + tag 16 bytes), "alg": "AES-256-GCM"}. AES key = SHA-256 of this key. Python: AESGCM(sha256(key)).decrypt(raw[:12], raw[12:], None).
ui.encNo: This app cannot decrypt messages, so content encryption is not available. Messages are still encrypted in transit (HTTPS / TLS); use Private mode to leave details out.
ui.encSignal: Signal is already end-to-end encrypted between signal-cli and your phone.
ui.ev_app_unhealthy: App crashed, keeps restarting or is unhealthy
ui.ev_vuln_found: New vulnerabilities in app images (Trivy scan)
ui.githubTokenLabel: GitHub Token (Optional — avoids rate limits & supports private repos)
ui.hintAutoRemoveMsg: Docker deletes a --rm container as soon as it stops, so AppManager cannot keep the old container for a safe rollback while updating or changing it. It is shown and can be started / stopped. To manage it fully, run it again without --rm (or with a docker-compose.yml).
ui.hintCardAutoRemove: Started with --rm — view, start and stop only
ui.hintCardExternal: Managed by another tool — view, start and stop only
ui.hintCardNotCompose: Created with docker run — can convert to compose
ui.hintCardNotMounted: Compose file not readable — tap to fix
ui.hintExternalMsg: Its labels show it belongs to an orchestrator or platform (Docker Swarm, Kubernetes, Unraid, Synology, Portainer agent…). That tool would overwrite any change AppManager makes, so AppManager only shows it and can start, stop and restart it. Update it from that tool.
ui.hintMountMsg: Mount this folder into AppManager at the same path (add it under volumes: of AppManager), or use the data folder setup to add it automatically:
ui.hintNotComposeMsg: AppManager manages apps through docker-compose.yml. A docker-compose.yml can be generated from this container's current settings (image, ports, volumes, environment, devices…). Review it below; nothing changes until you convert.
ui.hintNotMountedMsg: The container was created from this compose file on the host, but the folder is not mounted into AppManager, so update, edit and restore are disabled:
ui.hintPortainerMsg: The stack's compose file is inside the Portainer container ({path}) but no running Portainer container with a /data mount was found, so its location on the host is unknown. Start Portainer, then reload.
ui.hintPortainerNote: This is a Portainer stack: its compose files live in Portainer's data volume. AppManager runs it with the stack's real project name and stack.env.
ui.hintTitleExternal: This container is managed by another tool
ui.hintTitleNotCompose: This container was created with docker run
ui.hintTitleNotMounted: AppManager cannot see this app's docker-compose file
ui.hintTitlePortainer: Portainer stack: Portainer's data folder was not found
ui.holdLevel: {kind} {to} — waiting for you to update by hand
ui.holdUnknown: Version unknown — waiting for you to update by hand
ui.imageInUseTitle: This image is also used by other containers:
ui.imageInUseWhy: Docker cannot delete an image that a container uses, and forcing it would leave those apps broken on their next start or update.
ui.imageKeepOptDesc: recommended; the other apps keep working
ui.imageRemoveUsersOptDesc: their containers are removed (their AppData is kept), then the image is deleted
ui.imageRemoveUsersSelf: not possible: AppManager itself uses this image
ui.langHelpDesc: Missing text is shown in English. Improve a translation or add your language on GitHub.
ui.langPageNote: Applies right away on this device.
ui.logCapped: only the newest 50,000 lines were read — choose a shorter range
ui.logLiveHint: Live: new lines appear as they are written. Choose a time range to search older logs. Search: several words = all of them, -word = hide.
ui.logSearchHelp: Several words = lines with all of them; -word = hide lines with that word
ui.loginDeleteMsg: AppManager goes back to anonymous requests for this registry; private images from it can no longer be checked or pulled.
ui.nf_recipients: Recipients (numbers or group IDs, comma separated)
ui.nh_apprise: Apprise API (caronc/apprise in Docker) reaches 100+ services: WhatsApp, LINE, SMS, Rocket.Chat, Home Assistant… Enter Apprise URLs, or the key of a configuration saved in Apprise.
ui.nh_bark: iPhone only: install Bark from the App Store, copy the key from its URL (https://api.day.app/<key>/…). Leave the server empty for api.day.app or use your own Bark server.
ui.nh_discord: Discord channel → Edit channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy URL.
ui.nh_email: Gmail / Outlook: use an app password (2-step verification on). Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, STARTTLS 587. Outlook: smtp-mail.outlook.com, STARTTLS 587.
ui.nh_googlechat: Google Chat space → Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook → copy the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
ui.nh_gotify: Gotify → Apps → Create application → copy its Token.
ui.nh_matrix: Use a bot account: Element → Settings → Help & About → Access Token (or log in via the API). Invite the bot to the room; Room ID is in Room settings → Advanced.
ui.nh_mattermost: Mattermost → Integrations → Incoming Webhooks → Add → choose a channel → copy the URL. Rocket.Chat incoming webhooks work here too.
ui.nh_ntfy: Install the ntfy app (iPhone, Android, web) and subscribe to a hard-to-guess topic. Leave the server empty for ntfy.sh, or use your own server (Token if it requires login). Own server + iPhone: add upstream-base-url: "https://ntfy.sh" to its server.yml so iPhones get instant notifications (only a wake-up signal goes through ntfy.sh).
ui.nh_pushbullet: pushbullet.com → Settings → Account → Create Access Token. Mainly Android and web browsers.
ui.nh_pushover: pushover.net: your User Key is on the dashboard; create an Application to get its API Token. Apps for iPhone, Android and desktop (one-time purchase).
ui.nh_signal: Needs signal-cli-rest-api (bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api) running in Docker with a registered number. Server = its address.
ui.nh_slack: Slack → Apps → Incoming Webhooks → Add to Slack → choose a channel → copy the Webhook URL.
ui.nh_teams: Teams channel → ⋯ → Workflows → "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received" → copy the URL (Office 365 connectors are retired).
ui.nh_telegram: Create a bot with @BotFather to get the Token; send it a message, then get your chat ID with @userinfobot (groups: add the bot and use the group ID).
ui.nh_webhook: AppManager POSTs JSON {event, title, message, data, time}. With a secret, the X-AppManager-Signature header holds sha256=HMAC of the body.
ui.nh_webpush: Turn it on per device in the Web Push box above; this channel chooses which events are pushed to all those devices.
ui.noBackups: No backups created yet. Backups are auto-saved before every edit.
ui.noChangelog: Enter a GitHub repository (owner/repo or URL) to load Releases, CHANGELOG.md, or recent commits:
ui.noChangelogView: No changelog found for this app.
ui.noComposeWarning: No docker-compose.yml detected for this container.
ui.noTagsFound: No tags found for this image.
ui.noUpdateLog: No log was saved for this update.
ui.noUpdatesNow: No app has an update right now.
ui.notifyChannelsDesc: Get a message when updates are found, an update fails or is rolled back, an app crashes, the disk is almost full, or something happens to your account.
ui.notifyCriticalHint: important — also sent during quiet hours
ui.notifyDeleteMsg: AppManager stops sending notifications to this channel.
ui.notifyDiskPct: Warn when the disk is used above (%)
ui.notifyQuietDesc: Regular messages (updates found / done) wait and arrive as one summary afterwards; important ones are always sent.
ui.npApprise: Depends on the services you send to through Apprise (WhatsApp, LINE, SMS…).
ui.npNoIosHint: No iPhone app — on iPhone choose ntfy, Bark, Pushover or Telegram.
ui.npWebhook: Sends JSON to your own server or automation (Home Assistant, n8n, Node-RED…).
ui.pinnedTagCompose: Pinned tag detected — updating will bump docker-compose.yml to {tag} (with automatic backup).
ui.pinnedTagRun: Pinned tag detected — updating recreates the container from :{tag} with the same settings.
ui.polGlobalOff: Scheduled auto-update is off in Settings → General, so this app will not update by itself until you turn it on.
ui.polNote: Rules apply to automatic updates only — tapping Update still updates right away.
ui.polTimeDesc: Empty = the shared auto-update time ({t}). Missed while the server was off? It runs later that day.
ui.polWaitDesc: Days after AppManager first saw the new version — others find the bugs first.
ui.pol_all_desc: Every new version, including major ones (e.g. 1.x → 2.0).
ui.pol_minor_desc: Only within the same major version (e.g. 1.4 → 1.5); major upgrades wait for you.
ui.pol_patch_desc: Only fixes (e.g. 1.4.2 → 1.4.3); minor and major upgrades wait for you.
ui.privDesc: Send only a short title (e.g. "Update failed") without app names, IP addresses or details — open AppManager to see them. Works with every channel.
ui.pruneAllUnusedImages: Remove ALL unused images (not just dangling layers)
ui.pruneContainersWarn: This deletes every stopped container, including apps you stopped on purpose. Their data folders are kept; recreate them from their compose file.
ui.pruneOldImagesDesc: Free SSD space right after each successful update
ui.pruneVolumesWarn: Warning: data inside unused volumes will be permanently deleted.
ui.pwNote: Other devices will be signed out.
ui.pwTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters
ui.registryLoginsDesc: Optional. Raises Docker Hub limits and lets AppManager check and pull private images (Docker Hub, GHCR, own registry). The account is tested before it is saved.
ui.registryTokenHint: Use a read-only access Token, not your password: Docker Hub → Account settings → Personal access tokens (Read-only); GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Tokens (read:packages).
ui.releaseChannelDesc: Switching changes the image tag in docker-compose.yml and runs a normal update (health check + automatic rollback).
ui.restoreAppMsg: Select the backup to restore (default: latest). The image, docker-compose.yml and config files captured at backup time are restored. Other data, media and logs are skipped. The container is restarted afterwards.
ui.restoreAppMsgRun: Select the backup to restore (default: latest). The image, the container settings and the config files captured at backup time are restored; the container is recreated (even if it was deleted). Other data, media and logs are skipped.
ui.restoreBackupMsg: The container is stopped and config files are overwritten from the backup (current files are moved to "<folder>.pre-restore"). Other data, media and logs are skipped. The image and docker-compose.yml captured at backup time are restored if the image is still available on the host. The container is restarted afterwards.
ui.restoreRunning: Stopping the container, restoring config files, image and docker-compose.yml (the previous image is pulled from the registry if it was removed), then restarting the container…
ui.restoreRunningRun: Stopping the container, restoring config files and the image (pulled again if it was removed), then recreating the container from the saved settings…
ui.role_admin_desc: Everything: settings, accounts, API Tokens, servers, edit / deploy / uninstall apps.
ui.role_operator_desc: View + check for and install updates (also switch channel / version), start / stop / restart apps, restore backups, per-app update rules.
ui.role_viewer_desc: View apps, versions, changelogs, logs and update history. Cannot change anything.
ui.runBadgeTitle: Created with docker run — managed directly (recreated with the same settings on update)
ui.runCommandHelp: Equivalent docker run command for this container's current settings (what AppManager uses when it recreates it):
ui.runEditNote: No compose file: these are the container's current settings. Save & Apply recreates the container with the new settings (volumes and data are kept) and checks it; if it does not start, the previous container is started again.
ui.runEditPath: docker run container — settings read from the container
ui.runNoEdit: docker run container — use docker run command, or convert to compose to edit
ui.runUpdateNote: docker run container: updating pulls the new image, keeps the old container stopped and renamed, creates a new one with the same settings (ports, volumes, environment, networks…) and removes the old one only after the new one runs correctly; otherwise the old one is started again.
ui.setConfigDesc: Save / restore AppManager settings in one encrypted file
ui.setStorageDesc: Data folders, SSD cleanup, app backups
ui.setUsersDesc: Several people, each with their own role
ui.ssoAccountDesc: Your password and two-factor sign-in are managed by your identity provider. Your role follows your groups there.
ui.ssoAutoCreateDesc: First sign-in creates the AppManager account. Off: only accounts an admin created (with linking on) can sign in.
ui.ssoEnableDesc: Shows a "Sign in with …" button on the login page.
ui.ssoGroupsDesc: Group names from the provider, separated by commas. The highest matching role wins; it is updated at every sign-in.
ui.ssoLink: Link existing accounts with the same name
ui.ssoLinkDesc: Only turn on if the provider controls user names (users cannot pick any name), otherwise someone could take over an account.
ui.ssoPublicUrlDesc: Leave empty to use the address in your browser. Set it when the provider must send people back to another address.
ui.ssoRedirectNote: Must match exactly. If you open AppManager through another address (reverse proxy, Tailscale…), set "AppManager address" under Advanced.
ui.ssoSafety: Password sign-in always keeps working, so you cannot lock yourself out. Security: PKCE, state and nonce; issuer, audience and expiry are checked; RS256 signatures are verified with the provider keys.
ui.ssoSecretKept: Saved — leave empty to keep it
ui.ssoStep1: At the provider, create an OpenID Connect / OAuth2 application (confidential client, Authorization Code).
ui.ssoStep2: Paste the Redirect URI below into that application.
ui.ssoStep3: Copy its Issuer URL, Client ID and Client Secret here, press Test, then turn SSO on and Save.
ui.ssoStep4: Fill in which provider groups get Admin / Update / View only. Make the groups claim part of the token (e.g. Keycloak: Group Membership mapper; Authentik: profile scope).
ui.ssoTestDropped: Not supported by this provider, will be skipped: {s}
ui.ssoVerifyTlsDesc: Turn off only for a self-signed certificate inside your home network.
ui.ssoWhat: People sign in with the account they already have at your identity provider (Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak, Pocket ID, Zitadel, Google, Microsoft…) using OpenID Connect. Their AppManager role comes from their groups at the provider.
ui.ssoWhatTitle: Sign in with your identity provider
ui.svAllNote: Apps of this server and every added server in one list. Each card shows which server it is on; actions run on that server.
ui.svDeleteMsg: it is removed from this AppManager only; nothing changes on that machine. Also delete its API Token there if you no longer need it.
ui.svHttpWarn: HTTP is not encrypted: use it only inside your home network or a VPN. Over the Internet use HTTPS.
ui.svJobNote: You can close this window; the update keeps running on the other server and appears in its History.
ui.svJob_failed: Failed — see the log (rolled back if possible)
ui.svLoading: Loading apps from the other server…
ui.svNoBackups: {app} has no configuration backup on that server yet.
ui.svProtoDesc: this AppManager calls the REST API of the AppManager on the other machine over HTTP or HTTPS, signed with an API Token (Authorization: Bearer). The Docker socket is never opened to the network and nothing else needs to be installed.
ui.svRemoteNote: Edit Config and uninstall: open that server's AppManager (Open ↗). Logs and restore need AppManager 0.21 or newer there.
ui.svReqDesc: the other machine runs AppManager 0.17.0 or newer, and this machine can reach its address and port (same LAN, a VPN such as Tailscale / WireGuard, or HTTPS through a reverse proxy).
ui.svSavedOffline: Saved, but the server is not reachable right now
ui.svSecDesc: over the Internet always use HTTPS — plain HTTP sends the Token unencrypted. The Token is stored in this machine's database and never shown again.
ui.svStopMsg: The container on {server} stops until you start it again.
ui.svTokDesc: on the other machine open Settings → API Token and create a Token with the "Update" permission (update, restart) or "Read only" (view only). Limit it to the IP of this machine.
ui.svToken: API Token of the other server
ui.svTokenHint: Created on the other server: Settings → API Token (Update permission).
ui.svTokenKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved Token
ui.svUpdateAllMsg: {n} app(s) with an update, one after another, each with a health check and automatic rollback.
ui.svUpdateMsg: {server} downloads the new version ({from} → {to}), recreates the container, checks that it starts and rolls back by itself if it fails.
ui.svUrlHint: The address you open in the browser for that AppManager, with the port.
ui.svVerifyDesc: Turn off only for a self-signed certificate on a network you trust.
ui.svWorkDesc: the other machine still pulls, recreates, health-checks and rolls back by itself; this machine only sends the command and shows the result. Both activity logs record it.
ui.switchChannelMsg: Config files are backed up first; on failure the previous image and docker-compose.yml are restored.
ui.switchToPreMsg: Pre-release builds may be unstable and may migrate data in a way the stable version cannot read.
ui.switchToStableMsg: Returning to the stable channel can be an older version than the pre-release; config files backed up before the switch are restored if it fails to start.
ui.switchVariantMsg: This is a different image variant (e.g. -full has extra optional libraries, the plain one is smaller): some features may differ; test channels (dev / beta) only show if that variant has them.
ui.tfaCodesNote: Save these backup codes somewhere safe. Each code works once if you lose your phone. They will not be shown again.
ui.tfaDesc: Require a 6-digit code from an authenticator app when signing in
ui.tfaStep1: 1. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, iOS Passwords…) or enter the key manually.
ui.tfaStep2: 2. Enter the 6-digit code shown in the app:
ui.tkDeleteMsg: it stops working immediately; programs using it will get "401 Unauthorized". This cannot be undone.
ui.tkExKuma: Monitor type: HTTP(s) - Keyword. No Token needed for this URL.
ui.tkExUpdate: update an app (runs in the background, returns a job)
ui.tkFullDesc: Everything in the app, except your account, 2FA, API Tokens and registry passwords.
ui.tkHowUse: Use it in the header: Authorization: Bearer <Token>. Lost it? Delete it and create a new one.
ui.tkIntro: Tokens let other programs use AppManager without your password: Home Assistant, Scripts / CI, Uptime Kuma. Send it in the header Authorization: Bearer amp_…. Each Token can be removed at any time.
ui.tkIpsHint: IP addresses or networks, separated by commas. Empty = any address.
ui.tkOnce: Copy it now: this Token is shown only once. AppManager keeps only a fingerprint of it and cannot show it again.
ui.tkReadDesc: See apps, versions, updates, history and health. Cannot change anything.
ui.tkUpdateDesc: Read + check for updates, update an app or all apps (with health check and rollback), start / stop / restart, restore an app configuration backup.
ui.uiAppIconNote: To change the icon already on your Home Screen, remove AppManager from the Home Screen and add it again (iPhone keeps the old icon).
ui.uiDeviceNote: Saved on this device only. Tap Save below to keep the changes.
ui.unStepImageDesc: Free SSD storage used by this image
ui.upBackupsKept: AppManager's backups of this app are kept (Settings).
ui.upCasaDelete: Delete the CasaOS app folder (docker-compose.yml). The app disappears from CasaOS.
ui.upDataDelete: PERMANENTLY delete the data in {path}. This cannot be undone.
ui.upDataKeep: Keep the data in {path} (a reinstall reuses it).
ui.upDataShared: This folder is also used by {list}: those apps will lose data.
ui.upImageDelete: Delete the image {image} to free disk space. A reinstall downloads it again.
ui.upImageKeep: Keep the image {image} on disk (fast reinstall, no download).
ui.upImageKeepUsed: Keep the image: it is still used by {list} (deleting it would break those apps).
ui.upImageRemoveUsers: Also uninstall {list} (containers only; their AppData is kept), then delete the image.
ui.upStackOthers: Only this service is removed. {n} other service(s) of stack "{project}" ({list}) keep running.
ui.upStop: Stop and delete the container {name}. The app stops working.
ui.updateAllSkippedNote: ({n} app(s) skipped by your Update All settings.)
ui.updatingWait: Updating... Please keep this window open
ui.usDeleteMsg: This person can no longer sign in. Their past actions stay in the activity log.
ui.usDisableDesc: Cannot sign in until enabled again; signed out everywhere now.
ui.usNote: There is always at least one active Admin. Every action is recorded under the person who did it (Security → Activity log).
ui.usResetPh: Leave empty to keep the current password
ui.usSsoNote: SSO account: the role follows the provider groups at every sign-in; the password is managed by the provider.
ui.usWillOther: Save the changes. If the role, password or status changes, this person is signed out on every device and signs in again with the new settings.
ui.usWillSelf: Save the changes for your own account. You stay signed in on this device; your other devices are signed out.
ui.versionPickerMsg: Recent stable versions from the registry (same variant as the running image). Pick one to see its changelog first; nothing changes until you tap the update button.
ui.versionPreviewNote: Version :{tag} selected. The changelog below is for this version. Nothing is changed until you tap the update button: config files are backed up, the tag in docker-compose.yml is changed, then a normal update runs (health check + automatic rollback).
ui.versionPreviewNoteRun: Version :{tag} selected. The changelog below is for this version. Nothing is changed until you tap the update button: the image is pulled, the container is recreated with the same settings and checked; on failure the previous container is started again.
ui.viewOnlyNote: Your account can view only. Ask an administrator to update or change apps.
ui.vulnAcceptDesc: Accept the current vulnerabilities: the shield on the card is hidden and you are only notified again when new ones appear.
ui.vulnAccepted: Accepted — only new vulnerabilities will be shown
ui.vulnAcceptedInfo: {n} accepted on {t} by {u}. Only new vulnerabilities show the shield and send a notification.
ui.vulnAfterUpdate: Scan again after an app update
ui.vulnAfterUpdateDesc: Checks the new image right after it is pulled.
ui.vulnCardBadge: Show the shield on app cards
ui.vulnCardBadgeDesc: Off: results stay here and in the ⋯ menu only.
ui.vulnDoNetwork: Most of these are in bundled system libraries and matter mainly when the app is reachable from the internet. Keeping it inside your home network or behind a VPN (Tailscale) lowers the risk the most.
ui.vulnDoOwner: Only the developer of {app} can fix these: they update the packages inside and publish a new image. You do not need to (and should not) patch the container yourself.
ui.vulnDoUpdate: Version {v} is available: updating often fixes many of them, and AppManager scans again right after the update.
ui.vulnDoWait: Update when a new version comes out (or turn on Auto-Update); AppManager scans again after every update.
ui.vulnEnableDesc: On a schedule, after each app update, with a notification for new findings ("New vulnerabilities" event).
ui.vulnFixable: Only count vulnerabilities with a fix
ui.vulnFixableDesc: Ignore ones nobody can fix yet.
ui.vulnHint: With a fix: update the app when a new image is out. No fix yet: wait for the developer — it mostly matters if that component is used and reachable from outside.
ui.vulnIntro: AppManager uses Trivy (open source, by Aqua Security) to compare the software packages inside each app image with public vulnerability databases (CVE). It only reads the images — apps and data are not changed. "Fixed in" means the app developer has to publish a new image; updating the app then removes the problem.
ui.vulnNeedInstall: An administrator can install Trivy in Settings → Vulnerability Scan.
ui.vulnNotInstalled: Not installed. Needs about 200 MB (Trivy + vulnerability database), taken from the official aquasec/trivy image (ARMv7: GitHub).
ui.vulnNotScanned: This app has not been scanned yet.
ui.vulnOffDesc: Off · check app images for known vulnerabilities (Trivy)
ui.vulnSeveritiesDesc: Shown on app cards and notified when new ones appear.
ui.vulnUninstallMsg: Deletes the Trivy program and its vulnerability database from the data folder. Scan results are kept; you can install it again any time.
ui.vulnWhatTitle: Found in a third-party image — what can you do?
ui.wpBlocked: Notifications are blocked for this site in the browser / iPhone settings. Allow them there, then reload.
ui.wpDeleteMsg: This device stops receiving push notifications. It can turn them on again later.
ui.wpDenied: Permission was not given — allow notifications for this site and try again
ui.wpDesc: Straight to this browser or the AppManager icon on your home screen. No extra app needed.
ui.wpEnabled: Push notifications turned on for this device
ui.wpEventsNote: Which events are pushed: open the Web Push channel in the list below (created automatically).
ui.wpHttpsNote: Push notifications reach your devices anywhere; only turning them on needs the HTTPS address.
ui.wpHttps_cloudflare_desc: Cloudflare Zero Trust → Tunnels: run cloudflared, add a public hostname → http://<server IP>:<AppManager port>. Protect it with Cloudflare Access because it is reachable from the internet.
ui.wpHttps_proxy: 2. Reverse proxy with your own domain
ui.wpHttps_proxy_desc: Nginx Proxy Manager, Caddy or Traefik: point a domain (e.g. appmanager.example.com) to http://<server IP>:<AppManager port>, turn on SSL (Let's Encrypt) and WebSockets. Add the proxy IP to TRUSTED_PROXIES.
ui.wpHttps_tailscale_desc: In the Tailscale admin console turn on MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates. On the server run the command below (8098 = AppManager port), then open https://<server>.<tailnet>.ts.net on your phone with Tailscale on.
ui.wpIosDesc: In Safari tap Share → Add to Home Screen, open AppManager from that icon, then come back here and turn notifications on (iOS 16.4 or newer).
ui.wpIosTitle: iPhone: add AppManager to the Home Screen first
ui.wpNeedHttpsDesc: Browsers only allow push notifications on pages opened with https:// (this page uses http://). Open AppManager through HTTPS with one of the ways below, then turn it on there.
ui.wpTitle: Web Push — Notifications on browsers & phones
ui.wpUnsupported: This browser does not support push notifications.

login.accountDisabled: This account is disabled. Ask an administrator to enable it again.
login.adminExists: This machine already has an administrator. The administrator account can only be created right after AppManager is installed — ask the administrator for an account.
login.loginSubtitle: Sign in to manage containers, compose files & updates
login.noAccountYet: This machine has no account yet — create the administrator account in the Create account tab.
login.otherMachineDesc: Each machine running AppManager has its own accounts. Ask the administrator of that machine for an account, or for an API Token so you can add it under Settings → Servers here.
login.otpHint: 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or a backup code
login.pullHint: Press the power button to start
login.remember: Keep me signed in for 30 days
login.setupNote: This machine has no account yet. The first account is the administrator (full access): it can add other accounts, give them roles and turn on single sign-on.
login.setupSubtitle: Create an administrator account to protect your Docker engine
login.signupAdminDesc: This machine already has an administrator. To protect the Docker server, AppManager has no open password sign-up: ask the administrator to create your account (Settings → Accounts & Permissions).
login.signupAdminTitle: Accounts are created by an administrator
login.ssoErrConnect: Cannot connect to {host}: check the address and the network of AppManager.
login.ssoErrExists: An AppManager account named {user} already exists. An administrator can turn on "Link existing accounts with the same name" in the SSO settings.
login.ssoErrExpired: Sign-in expired or was started in another tab — please try again.
login.ssoErrGroup: {user} is not in a group allowed to use AppManager (groups: {groups}). Ask an administrator.
login.ssoErrNoAccount: There is no AppManager account for {user} (automatic account creation is off). Ask an administrator.
login.ssoOffHint: Google, Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia… can be turned on by an administrator in Settings → Single sign-on.
login.ssoSignupNote: Your account is created the first time you sign in; your role follows your groups.

notify.n_test_body: You'll get alerts on this device.
notify.private_body: Open AppManager Pro to see the details.
notify.sec_ip_locked: IP {ip} was locked for 15 minutes after repeated failed logins (user: {user}).
notify.sec_token_new: A new API token "{name}" ({scope}) was created by {user} (IP {ip}).
notify.test_body: AppManager Pro can reach this channel.
